newsitem.title: FRANCE: INTERVIEW-Accor reaffirms forecast for profit rise.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Accor reaffirms forecast for profit rise.

text.p: Accor chairman Jean-Marc Espalioux said on Wednesday that the hotel business was looking better in Europe and he reaffirmed his forecast for a profit rise this year.
He said in an interview with Reuters that the rise of the dollar and sterling against the French franc were "very favourable" for the group.
Conversely, a planned increase in French tax on corporate profits would have only a small impact, he said.

"Based on the figures we had at the end of July, we confirm the results forecast made at the start of June for a rise in pre-tax, pre-exceptional profit of more than 20 percent," Espalioux told Reuters.

"As for net profit, it will show a significant rise, as a function of pre-tax, pre-exceptional profit, of the capital gain from the sale of Compass shares of around one billion francs and provisions set after a detailed review of the assets, notably the hotel assets, begun two months ago."
Accor on Wednesday reported an 8.3 percent rise in turnover for the six months to June 30 to 15 billion francs, with 3.3 percent due to the impact of currency movements.

Turnover from the main hotel business was up 14.3 percent, with 3.6 percent due to favourable currency movements. At a constant structure, the rise was 4.8 percent, with growth accelerating from 3.5 percent in the first quarter to 6.1 percent in the second.

"The hotel business in Europe is improving generally, with particularly favourable trends in Britain, Italy, Spain and central Europe, Hungary especially, to a slightly lesser extent in France... with Germany bringing up the rear," Espalioux said.
He said the German hotel business was saddled with excess capacity that weighed on prices.

He added that Europe's economy still has soft spots. "When we say that Europe's economic condition is improving, we have to underscore that the improvement is modest in France and uncertain in Germany," Espalioux added.

"As for the evolution of the pound sterling and dollar, the impact is very favourable as it increases the value for us of results in our companies based in the United States, such as Motel 6, in Britain and in countries whose currencies are linked to the dollar, notably Brazil and Argentina," he said.
He said the currencies' gains were also helping Accor, notably its Paris hotels, by encouraging more tourism in France.
Competition is tough in the budget hotel segment in the United States, but Motel 6 is performing in line with targets set in its 1997 budget, Espalioux said.
He said the renovation of half the 750 motels had allowed the U.S. unit to raise prices, more than offsetting the negative impact of sluggish occupancy rates.

Overall, "the (first-half sales) figures are encouraging for us just as our Accor 2000 programme gets under way. I am confident," said Espalioux, who was appointed chairman of the management board in October after co-founders Paul Dubrule and Gerard Pelisson decided to give up the day-to-day management. They now head the supervisory board.

The Accor 2000 reorganisation plan, aimed at boosting growth and synergies, got under way in June with the appointment of key managers in a sweeping drive affecting some 200-250 posts, Espalioux said.

He reiterated his expectation that Accor 2000 would have an impact on results from the second half of 1998. "In 1998 we expect a further 150-200 million franc ($31.4 million) improvement in results over the normal trend," he said.
Accor reported a 14.6 percent profit rise for 1996 to 1.06 billion francs and brought its debt in line with equity -- a balance which Espalioux said he sought to maintain.
In March it sold an 11.5 percent stake in British food service provider Compass Group Plc.
The review of the hotel assets under way will determine which are kept, which are sold or refinanced through the sale of the walls while keeping the hotels under management.
-- Christine Tierney, Paris Newsroom, +33 1 4221 5452 ($ = 6.379 French Francs)
